problemStatement.formal: Define triangular, pentagonal, and hexagonal figurate numbers, prove the triangular reciprocal partial fraction identity, and verify convergence-supporting reciprocal facts.
problemStatement.plain: Extend the triangular-reciprocal story to higher figurate numbers by formalizing basic figurate definitions, examples, telescoping identities, and square-reciprocal summability.
whyMatters: Triangular reciprocal sums are a clean example of telescoping via partial fractions.
Figurate-number definitions make the reciprocal-sum question extensible beyond triangles.
The square-reciprocal summability result supplies the comparison-theorem backbone for broader convergence claims.

proven: The triangular reciprocal partial fraction identity 2/(n(n+1)) = 2/n - 2/(n+1) is proved for n >= 1 (Lean: partial_fraction).
Triangular reciprocal terms are positive for positive n (Lean: triangular_reciprocal_pos).
Triangular, pentagonal, and hexagonal number functions are defined and checked on initial values (Lean: triangular, pentagonal, hexagonal, triangular_values, pentagonal_values, hexagonal_values).
Triangular numbers grow at least linearly and hexagonal numbers are identified with a triangular subsequence (Lean: triangular_ge_n, hexagonal_eq_triangular).
The reciprocal square series is proved summable, giving the p-series comparison model for figurate reciprocal convergence (Lean: square_reciprocals_summable).
knownResults.goal: Document the verified figurate-number reciprocal lemmas and convergence-supporting facts.
